1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating token.sessionId === session.id in /api/verify-token.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because tokens are bound to sessionId and mockAccountHash.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after password reset (session.resetComplete = true, and old sessions are deleted after 30 minutes).

4.why: The website uses HTTPS with TLS (Bun.serve with tls config) and enforces HSTS via headers.

5.why: Reset codes are encrypted (sha256 hashed) and user data is not exposed in plaintext.

6.why: Email messages (simulated logs) do not expose private user data; only mock tokens are shown.

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is validated via validIdentifier and passwordPolicy functions.

8.why: Redirect links are only to the hospital’s site (/verify) and are hardcoded or validated.

9.why: Email templates (simulated logs) contain no scripts or HTML from user input; only text is used.

10.why: Private information or tokens are not shown in error pages or logs (generic messages only).

11.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (Bun.password.hash), and no secrets are stored in code.

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials; all sessions require CSRF and validation.

13.why: The system bars excessive wrong attempts via rate limiting (consumeRateLimit, recordVerificationFailure).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (generic response in /api/recovery-request).

15.why: Password reset codes are random (randomValue(32)), complex, and user-specific (bound to sessionId).
